title: How to claim flight compensation fast when disruption strikes
summary: What actually speeds up a flight compensation claim — and what slows it down. Straight answers, no legalese. Start your claim free.
body_markdown:
If your flight was delayed, canceled, or you were bumped off it entirely, the fastest way to get paid up to €600 isn't a legal trick — it's getting a complete claim in quickly, through one channel, before the airline's queue backs up.


Most of what slows a claim down isn't the law. It's incomplete evidence, submitting the same claim two different ways with different companies, or simply getting caught in a backlog when a storm, an ATC restriction, or a holiday-travel spike hits a lot of flights at once. Here's what actually moves the needle.


## How claiming actually works


Once you submit a claim, it goes through three stages. First, eligibility verification — checking your flight against the disruption and confirming it qualifies under EC 261. This is usually the fastest part. Second, formal notice to the airline. Third, if the airline pushes back, escalation — negotiation, and if needed, legal proceedings.


The airline-negotiation stage is where most of the waiting happens, and it's slower during a disruption spike, when airlines are fielding a higher volume of claims at once than usual. That's true in July, but it's just as true during an autumn storm system or a strike week — it's about volume, not the calendar.

## The specifics: fee, coverage, process


You can be entitled to up to €600 under EC 261 for a delay, cancellation, or denied boarding — the exact figure depends on the length of your flight. AirHelp charges a 35% success fee taken directly from the compensation once it's secured. Nothing upfront. Nothing if the claim doesn't succeed.


Coverage runs across flight delays, cancellations, and denied boarding. If you want extra speed on top of a standard claim, you don't need a membership for it: the AirHelp app lets you add a standalone fast-track option when you add your trip, at a discounted rate, no AirHelp+ required.


## Who this is right for


This is for anyone whose flight got caught in a disruption spike — not just summer travelers. That includes storm-season delays, ATC or staffing-related restrictions, strike disruption, and holiday-peak congestion at any time of year. If you're looking for the reasons behind a specific stretch of disruption rather than how to claim quickly, our[piece on peak-summer delays](https://www.airhelp.com/en-int/blog/peak-summer-delays-why-july-and-august-are-the-worst-and-what-you-can-claim/) covers the causes in more depth.


Before you submit anything, it helps to[gather the right evidence at the airport](https://www.airhelp.com/en-int/blog/i-ve-missed-my-flight-what-are-my-rights-as-a-passenger/) — your booking reference, boarding pass, and a note of why the airline said you were delayed. A complete claim the first time is faster than a partial one you have to follow up on later.
